A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Iso-C/Iso-CTS research, with readable text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Shared content can be matched reliably despite the expanded experiments and reorganized appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-merging results on 8, 14, and 20 vision tasks in Table 1, together with original alignment analyses and ablations in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds LoRA and language-model evaluations, additional vision comparisons, interference measurements, and component ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the core spectral merging operations remain unchanged. Section 5.2 adds a limited input adaptation for LoRA: reconstruct each task update as Delta W_t = B_t A_t before applying the existing merging procedure. No substantial algorithm redesign or new training objective is introduced.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates vision tasks only. V2 adds language-model merging on 7-task and 8-task subsets of the T0 mixture (Section 5.3, Table 3), substantially extending domain and task coverage. The original vision datasets are retained; the LoRA experiments reuse the existing eight vision tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains its comparator set. New comparisons evaluate DARE-TIES, KnOTS-TIES, and KnOTS-DARE-TIES for LoRA (Table 2); Fisher Merging, RegMean, and MaTS for language models (Table 3); and additional vision baselines including PCB and CART (Table 4). These are evaluated comparators, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: V2 introduces rank-16 LoRA evaluations using KnOTS ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14 checkpoints, T5-Large-LM-Adapt language evaluations, and a separate vision comparison using Task Arithmetic checkpoints instead of the Consensus Merging checkpoints used in Table 1. Appendix D.2 also introduces mean L1 embedding distance as an interference measure. The retained Table 1 protocol and reported alpha choices are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of embedding interference (Appendix D.2, Figure 7), the necessity of isotropic scaling within Iso-CTS (D.4, Figure 8), alignment across transformer layers (E.2, Figure 13), and whether the alignment–performance relationship persists on ViT-L/14 (E.3, Figure 9). The earlier interpolation, subspace-size, alpha-sensitivity, and single-task flattening analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-level uncertainty. The retained boxplots summarize variation across tasks rather than repeated runs. The revised Pearson correlation value changes a result, not the statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 is numerically unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results: Iso-CTS scores 75.0/89.6 normalized accuracy for LoRA ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14 (Table 2), while Iso-C scores 75.6/83.3 absolute accuracy on the 8/7 NLP tasks (Table 3). Table 4 and the new analyses add further outcomes. Section 3.3 and Figure 3 revise the reported SAR–NAI correlation from 0.88 to 0.94. The added benchmark scores are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds theoretical appendices absent from v1: a spectral derivation of effective rank, a projection-based SAR monotonicity argument, an activation-interference decomposition, and a variance argument explaining underrepresented tasks (Appendix A). Appendix B adds an asymptotic SVD-cost comparison of Iso-C, Iso-CTS, and TSV-M. These additions go substantially beyond restating the existing method equations.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly claims state-of-the-art performance on language as well as vision tasks. A new introduction contribution asserts versatility across vision/language benchmarks and fully fine-tuned/LoRA models. This materially broadens the claimed applicability beyond v1's vision-only evidence, while retaining the original alignment and isotropic-merging contributions.

C2.justification: V2 develops activation preservation as an explanation for reduced interference, interprets similar Iso-C/Iso-CTS NLP performance as evidence that the common subspace is sufficient there, and explains when isotropic scaling matters within Iso-CTS. The conclusion replaces v1's vision-only limitation with the limitation that low-rank structure is not fully exploited; the potentially suboptimal Task Arithmetic common subspace remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: V2 supplies checkpoint sources, LoRA rank and reconstruction instructions, the language-model identity, and protocol references for the added evaluations. Existing vector-parameter averaging, the default common-subspace fraction, and the alpha table are retained. The same code URL remains, while v1's inconsistent statement promising a future release is removed; the PDFs do not establish a newly available resource.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantive distinction between static and dynamic merging, contrasting Twin-Merging and EMR-Merging and explicitly limiting its scope to static merging. References supporting the additional merging comparisons, language evaluations, interference analysis, and complexity analysis substantially expand the literature coverage. The updated publication details for TSV and KnOTS refer to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most introductory and methodological prose is retained. Local rewrites clarify cosine similarity and alignment terminology; Section 5 is reorganized around fully fine-tuned vision, LoRA, language, and analyses; and existing appendix material is redistributed under experimental details, experiments, and visualizations. Affiliations, publication text, and acknowledgements are also updated. These edits do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds dedicated tables for LoRA, NLP, and alternative-checkpoint vision comparisons, plus figures for interference, isotropic-scaling ablation, larger-model correlation, and per-layer alignment. Existing NAI plots have revised axes and Figure 3 has revised labeling. Earlier appendix plots and the alpha table are retained and relocated or renumbered, rather than removed.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's explicit vision-only limitation with language experiments and adds LoRA evidence and broader baseline comparisons. The new Iso-CTS scaling ablation and interference measurements more directly test the proposed mechanism, while the theoretical appendices clarify its rationale and computational cost. These gains substantially strengthen generality and explanatory support while preserving the earlier evidence. The interference argument remains approximate and uncertainty reporting is still absent, but these limitations do not outweigh the improvements.
